title: OIDC trusted publishing is broken by GitHub immutable subject claims
description: release.yml's publish job cannot authenticate to npm. GitHub issues immutable-format OIDC subject claims for this repository (repo:opum-ai@311910387/lore-cli@1365013937:...), and npm Trusted Publishing matches the classic repo:opum-ai/lore-cli:... form, so npm treats the token as unauthenticated and returns E404 on PUT. Proven by decoding a real token minted with audience npm:registry.npmjs.org in probe run 34787200768. Cause is GitHub's 2026-04-23 policy that every repository created after 2026-07-15 uses the immutable format; lore-cli was recreated 2026-09-10, one day after 0.6.0 published successfully from CI under the old repo id. quest-cli shows the same E404 and has confirmed use_immutable_subject true on its own repository, so the same mechanism is very likely in play there -- but it was recreated the same day and has a competing NODE_AUTH_TOKEN theory of its own, so do NOT restate this as 'broken identically' until one of us reads the registry's actual refusal message. quest-cli's theory is disproven in npm's source; see the reconciliation comment. Repo-level opt-out does not work: PUT to actions/oidc/customization/sub with use_immutable_subject false is accepted and has no effect. GitHub documents no opt-out once adopted. Until this is resolved every release must use the manual scripts/publish-release.sh path, which itself requires a human because npm demands a browser OTP that cannot be completed in a non-TTY. Full evidence and two documented false leads are on LCLI-475.

acceptanceCriteria.text: release.yml publish job successfully authenticates to npm via OIDC on a real publish:true dispatch, OR the job is removed/replaced with a documented manual-only path and release-publishing.md no longer presents OIDC as the working mechanism

release-publishing.md explains the immutable subject claim incompatibility, including that re-registering Trusted Publishers does not fix it and that the GITHUB_TOKEN Permissions log group omits IdToken even when granted
The npm-side limitation is reported upstream or a tracked upstream issue is linked, so this is not rediscovered from scratch

quest-cli is told the outcome and the reconciliation is settled in both trackers: either the shared cause is confirmed by the registry's own refusal message, or the two repos' causes are recorded as distinct -- rather than either side asserting the other's mechanism from a shared symptom

The publish step runs at NPM_CONFIG_LOGLEVEL=verbose (or --loglevel verbose) so npm's swallowed 'Failed token exchange request with body message' line is actually visible, since every diagnosis on this task so far is an inference from a downstream E404

release.yml's 'Assert no token is shadowing OIDC' guard keeps its check but loses its false mechanism: npm calls oidc() before reading credentials and overwrites _authToken on success, so a configured token does not prevent OIDC -- it becomes the silent fallback when the exchange fails

comments.body:
RECONCILED WITH quest-cli, 2026-09-13. This task's sentence "quest-cli is broken identically" was asserted without quest-cli's evidence, and quest-cli has since published a COMPETING root cause. I went and read npm's source rather than let either claim stand on authority. The immutable-subject diagnosis below SURVIVES; the "identically" wording does not, and is corrected in the description.

QUEST-CLI'S COMPETING CLAIM (QCLI-271 implementation note, from actions/setup-node@v6.0.0's source): setup-node with `registry-url` and no token unconditionally runs
    core.exportVariable('NODE_AUTH_TOKEN', process.env.NODE_AUTH_TOKEN || 'XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX')
so npm's .npmrc resolves `_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` to that placeholder and -- they concluded -- "authenticates with a fake token instead of ever attempting OIDC trusted publishing". Their fix (`unset NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` before npm publish) is merged to their dev as PR #39.

THAT CONCLUSION IS WRONG, and it is wrong in npm's code, not as a matter of opinion:
  - lib/commands/publish.js:152 calls `await oidc({...})` UNCONDITIONALLY, and does it BEFORE reading credentials at all -- getCredentialsByURI is line 154, after.
  - lib/utils/oidc.js contains NO early return on an existing _authToken. Its only bail-outs are: not a recognised CI vendor; ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL/TOKEN absent; no id_token; the exchange request threw; the exchange response carried no `.token`.
  - On success it OVERWRITES whatever .npmrc held:
        opts[authTokenKey] = response.token
        config.set(authTokenKey, response.token, 'user')
  - Verified identical in npm 12.0.2 (local) and npm 11.19.1 (packed fresh from the registry). The `^11` major is what this repo's publish job installs, so the version that matters is checked, not assumed.

EMPIRICAL CORROBORATION: this repo's release.yml has carried actions/setup-node with registry-url -- and therefore that exact placeholder -- since before v0.6.0. `git show v0.6.0:.github/workflows/release.yml` and HEAD have a byte-identical setup-node step. 0.6.0 PUBLISHED SUCCESSFULLY FROM CI with the placeholder present, and carries real SLSA provenance (opum-cli-e2e re-derived that from the registry independently). A cause that was present during a success is not the cause of the later failure.

WHAT QUEST-CLI ACTUALLY FOUND, which is real and worth keeping: the placeholder is a MASKING layer, not a cause. When the exchange fails, oidc() swallows it (log.verbose + return undefined) and npm falls back to .npmrc. With the placeholder that is a PUT with a fake token -> E404. Without it -> ENEEDAUTH. Same failure, better error. Their `unset` is a genuine diagnostic improvement; it will not make a publish succeed.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS REPO'S OWN WORKFLOW, and it is a real defect: the guard at release.yml "Assert no token is shadowing OIDC" states the same wrong mechanism -- "If NODE_AUTH_TOKEN holds a REAL token, npm authenticates with it and NEVER ATTEMPTS OIDC". Per the source above, npm attempts OIDC first regardless and overwrites the token on success. The guard is still WORTH KEEPING (a real token silently becomes the fallback when the exchange fails, so a publish can succeed under the wrong identity and without provenance, which is worse than failing) but its stated reasoning is false and its error text tells the reader something untrue. Fix the comment and the ::error:: wording; do not delete the check.

HIGHEST-VALUE UNTAKEN STEP, cheap: nobody has read the registry's own refusal. oidc.js logs it at verbose only --
    log.verbose('oidc', `Failed token exchange request with body message: ${error?.body?.message || 'Unknown error'}`)
Set NPM_CONFIG_LOGLEVEL=verbose (or --loglevel verbose on the publish step) and npm will print why the exchange was refused, in the registry's words, instead of us inferring it from an E404 three layers downstream. Every theory in this task so far -- mine and quest-cli's -- is an inference from that E404. Do this before the next dispatch.

METHOD NOTE worth more than the bug: both wrong claims here were produced the same way -- a mechanism inferred from a symptom, then asserted about a SECOND repository whose evidence the author had not seen. quest-cli inferred from setup-node's source without checking whether npm consults .npmrc before OIDC; this task inferred "identically" about quest-cli from a shared symptom. The check that settled it was reading the consuming code, not the producing code.
